items.question: Name the three federal branches and give the main job of each.
items.answer: Legislative (Congress) makes laws; executive (President and agencies) carries out laws; judicial (federal courts) interprets laws and decides constitutional cases.

items.question: What does federalism divide?
items.answer: It divides constitutional power between the national (federal) government and state governments; both can govern people directly within their assigned powers.

items.question: Why does federal supremacy not mean the federal government can regulate anything it wants?
items.answer: Federal law is supreme only when it is validly made under constitutional authority. Powers not delegated to the federal government, and not prohibited to states, are reserved to states or the people.

items.question: The federal minimum wage is one amount, and a state sets a higher minimum wage. Which level can set the higher rule, and why?
items.answer: The state can generally set a higher minimum wage. Federal law can establish a nationwide floor; a state may give workers greater protection, as long as its rule does not conflict with federal law.

items.question: What does separation of powers mean? Give its Simplified Chinese equivalent.
items.answer: It divides federal power among the legislative, executive and judicial branches. Chinese: 权力分立.

items.question: What does checks and balances mean? Give its Simplified Chinese equivalent.
items.answer: Each branch has powers that can limit or respond to the other branches. Chinese: 制衡机制.

items.question: What does federalism mean? Give its Simplified Chinese equivalent.
items.answer: It divides constitutional power between the national government and state governments. Chinese: 联邦制.
